source_snapshot.items: All SSD Slot Number Check - NVMe
source_snapshot.procedure: Insert all NVMe SSDs into backplane slots and check the NVMe-adapter slot numbers; collect photos and inspect logs.
source_snapshot.criteria: Slot numbering must match the system specification.
source_snapshot.deepseek: YES uses lsblk, /dev/nvme order and truncated nvme identify output, incorrectly treating a read-only device list as sufficient physical-slot evidence and omitting insertion risk.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: RPUC/CHANGED with HIGH physical/storage risk; require operator photos, stable serial-to-slot map and complete PCI/sysfs/NVMe topology instead of device-name order.

historical_reviews.deepseek: Collects useful identities but neither maps physical labels nor proves backplane slot numbers, and its insecure SSH/truncated output weakens evidence.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Adds full physical and logical topology correlation plus insertion, RAID/data and recovery controls.
historical_reviews.related_cases: The duplicate code at row433 tests E.1s PCIe vendor/device and Gen4 speed/width, not this all-NVMe physical slot-number population case.
historical_reviews.v3_1: This variant is governed by row85 and variant ID 559b9ba27bb926c3; code-only selection is unsafe.

original_test_intent: Verify that every approved NVMe SSD is physically installed in its specified backplane slot and that adapter/controller, PCIe and OS topology report the same platform-defined slot mapping.
original_method: A qualified operator inserts and photographs each stable-identity SSD at its labeled bay while the agent captures complete controller, PCIe/sysfs and NVMe namespace topology and compares the resulting one-to-one map with the approved specification.
manual_activity: User approves the population/topology map and duplicate-code identity; qualified operator inserts and photographs each SSD; agent collects and correlates the read-only topology.
required_inputs: Approved serial/WWN/NVMe ID to labeled backplane-slot matrix
Backplane, adapter, controller, PCIe root-port and namespace topology
Qualified operator, ESD controls, OOB/console and evidence location
safety_requirements: Dispatch by source row and variant ID, never by duplicate code alone
Verify every drive and slot identity before physical insertion
Do not infer slot number from /dev/nvme index, controller discovery order or namespace number
Preserve complete logs and stop on resistance, wrong slot, enumeration mismatch, RAID/filesystem/thermal/SEL event or access loss
Do not reseat, reorder, rebuild or reboot automatically
agent_execution_scope: Collect complete lsblk, nvme, lspci, sysfs physical-slot/PCI path, controller, RAID, mount and health evidence
Correlate operator photos and flag any unmapped or multiply mapped identity
Do not manipulate drives, infer physical labels, repair/rebuild or issue verdict
engineer_actions: Resolve the duplicate-code identity and approve the expected topology/population map
Provide a qualified operator and own data/RAID/recovery decisions
Review every physical/logical mapping and decide PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: lsblk and nvme identify assist stable identity, but /dev/nvme order and head-truncated controller data cannot establish a physical backplane slot; the command also omits PCIe/sysfs topology and operator evidence.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Securely capture untruncated lsblk, nvme list/id, lspci topology, sysfs PCI/physical-slot data and controller inventory, then join stable IDs to the operator's labeled-bay photos and approved platform map.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: All-NVMe insertion, adapter slot-number comparison and the source 15/8 timing fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Create a verified bipartite map between physical labeled bays and stable NVMe/controller/PCIe identities after the approved full population is installed.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds composite source identity, exact physical-to-logical correlation and storage-safety boundaries instead of trusting enumeration order.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Automation validates topology but cannot replace operator insertion and physical label evidence.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Linux device numbering is discovery-dependent and a namespace may not correspond one-to-one with a physical drive; controller and PCI paths plus serials are required.

project_override_considerations: If enclosure management exposes an authoritative slot property, it may strengthen but not replace the physical label/photo and stable-drive correlation unless the platform specification explicitly declares it authoritative.
expected_evidence: Duplicate-code resolution and approved row85 topology/population matrix
Operator/date, drive serial and labeled-slot photos

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The same code identifies row85 All SSD Slot Number Check - NVMe and row433 E.1s detect with PCIe Gen4 link criteria. Their purposes and evidence are materially different, so code-only identity is ambiguous and both variants must remain separate.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Composite source row and variant identity safely preserve this review. Physical mapping and insertion controls are supplyable prerequisites; execution is approval-gated rather than intrinsically blocked.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Compatibility row85 Wistron-Storage-00068-V002: assign or approve a unique identity distinct from row433 E.1s detect; provide the exact NVMe serial/WWN/NGUID-to-physical-slot/backplane/adapter/controller/BDF/root-port/namespace map, authoritative slot-number source, supported insertion/hot-swap or powered-off procedure, mount/RAID/boot/data protections, operator/photo evidence, abort, restoration and recovery rules. /dev/nvme enumeration order must not define physical slot identity.

review_improvement: Preserves this duplicate-code variant as a physical/logical slot-map test and requires stable topology plus operator evidence instead of discovery order.
independent_technical_reasoning: NVMe controller and namespace indices are assigned by discovery and can change across boots, while a drive can expose multiple namespaces. Therefore, slot correctness cannot be inferred from /dev names; it requires a join across stable drive identity, controller BDF/sysfs path, platform slot metadata and the operator's physical label record, with duplicate-code dispatch explicitly disambiguated.
